Unter einem losen Bremsklotz hat ein Trä: A porter hid his savings under a loose brake block. He never came back.
Ein Setzkasten, zugenagelt. Statt Letter: A type case, nailed shut. Instead of letters it holds things someone refused to pawn.
Die Kasse ohne Quittung: The cash box without a receipt
Eine Geldkassette ohne Beleg. Auf dem Ma: A cash box without a receipt. On the market that means it never existed.
Eine Kapsel, die seit Jahren im Rohr ste: A capsule stuck in the tube for years. The wasps guarded it as if they knew what was inside.
Unter den Laken, die nie trocknen, steht: Beneath the sheets that never dry stands a chest. The widows say it belongs to everyone who still comes back.
Ein Kasten mit dem Stempel „ausgesondert: A box stamped “discarded”. Only the inventory entry was discarded, not the contents.
Liebe Mara, oben haben sie mir die Haut: Dear Mara, up there they took my skin and my name along with it. Down here they call me “the Tuesday one”. I hope you still call me something else.
Wir setzen jeden Morgen die Namen der Ne: Every morning we set the names of the newcomers. By evening three of them are scratched out again. Nobody asks who collects the letters.
Ich schulde dem Pfandhaus meinen Mantel,: I owe the pawnshop my coat, the market my bread and the city my name. Only the last grows dearer every day.
Wer diese Kapsel findet: Die Rohre führe: Whoever finds this capsule: the tubes do not only lead up. One leads down, beneath the Crown Archive. Nothing is delivered there. Things are collected.
Sie sagen, mein Mann sei gestürzt. Ich h: They say my husband fell. I did not see him fall. I only saw his name vanish from the board, an hour before they told me.
Zwölf Namen, sauber durchgestrichen, all: Twelve names, neatly struck through, all in the same ink. In the margin, in another hand: “Not struck. Harvested.”
Mit Kreide auf ein Brett geschrieben: „I: Chalked on a board: “On every terrace one of us hid something before he was struck off. At the back of the alleys by the wall. Mind what lives there now.”
Unter dem Aushang liegt ein Umschlag mit: Under the notice lies an envelope with your name. The porters pay what they owed each other, to the one who found it all.
Ruth Malliver legt die sechs Briefe nebe: Ruth Malliver lays the six letters side by side and reads for a long time. “The ink is the same everywhere,” she says. “This is no accident. This is a list.” She gives you what the archive pays for evidence.
Gestrichene Träger haben in jeder Terras: Struck-off porters hid something on every terrace, at the back of the dead-end alleys by the north wall. Something now lives there and guards the hiding places.
Den Trägern am Aushang Bescheid geben: Tell the porters at the notice board
In den Gassen Calderwicks liegen angesen: Singed letters from the fallen lie in Calderwick's alleys. Together they tell where the struck-off go.
Die Briefe zu Ruth Malliver ins Archiv b: Bring the letters to Ruth Malliver in the archive
